project.name: medium
project.description: Medium is a multi-tenant SaaS scaffold that lets solo physical therapists manage patient bookings over WhatsApp with an AI assistant, overseen from a mobile-first PWA. It is built on Next.js App Router with Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui, with placeholder API routes for WhatsApp, Meta embedded auth, and Inngest still to be wired to live services.

nodes.name: engine.ts
nodes.summary: Central conversation orchestration engine for the WhatsApp assistant: loads conversation context, runs a multi-step LLM turn with tool-calling under an advisory lock, persists the reply, and routes to safety escalation, human handoff, or reminder-triggered turns as needed.
nodes.languageNotes: Every mutating turn runs inside a per-message Postgres advisory lock (withAdvisoryLock) so concurrent inbound webhooks for the same message cannot double-book or double-reply.

nodes.name: errors.ts
nodes.summary: Defines ConversationEngineError, a typed error carrying a closed set of engine failure codes (conversation not found/inactive, empty response, step limit reached, assistant paused) used to distinguish expected control-flow exits from real failures.

nodes.name: safety.ts
nodes.summary: Deterministic, regex-based detector for when a patient message must escalate to a human -- human requests, urgent health symptoms, legal/billing disputes, insurance questions, or high frustration -- tuned for both English and diacritic-variant Albanian text.
nodes.languageNotes: Folds Unicode combining marks and curly apostrophes before matching so Albanian diacritic variants (e/c) and mobile-keyboard punctuation quirks can't evade the safety patterns; patterns use Unicode letter lookarounds instead of ASCII word-boundary escapes for correct Albanian word boundaries.

nodes.name: admin.ts
nodes.summary: Cross-tenant operator metrics for the admin dashboard: signup/booking funnels, onboarding cohort, AI + Meta cost summaries, push-delivery health, plan distribution, conversion, renewal rate, downgrades, usage-cap hits, free-tier COGS, and recent POK payments, all queried with the RLS-bypassing owner connection.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately bypasses the tenancy/RLS layer (uses the bare db owner connection) because these queries must aggregate across every tenant; access is gated only by the admin page's ADMIN_EMAILS check, not by RLS.

nodes.name: queries.ts
nodes.summary: Read queries for a PT's configured services: listing active/inactive services, fetching one active service by ID or by name (case/whitespace-insensitive), and resolving the service to book from either a service ID or a legacy free-text service name.

nodes.name: smoke-ai.ts
nodes.summary: Standalone CLI smoke test that exercises the real OpenRouter/AI SDK pipeline end to end against a free-tier model, asserting the model calls a synthetic get_availability tool and returns final text before any live model can be marked healthy.

nodes.name: getOpenRouterStepMetadata
nodes.summary: Extracts the OpenRouter provider name and per-step cost from a generateText step's opaque providerMetadata payload.

nodes.name: runModelTurn
nodes.summary: Runs one LLM turn with tool-calling against the assistant tools, capping steps at STEP_LIMIT, and classifies the outcome as a final text response or a handoff-required result (empty response or step limit reached after a mutation).

nodes.name: loadContext
nodes.summary: Loads the full persisted context needed for a conversation turn (message, conversation, patient, and PT/practice fields) in one joined query via the service-role client.

nodes.name: findExistingReply
nodes.summary: Looks up an already-persisted AI reply to a given inbound message, used for idempotent retries so a turn is never answered twice.

nodes.name: loadHistory
nodes.summary: Loads and chronologically orders the recent conversation history (up to HISTORY_LIMIT messages) to feed the model as prior turns.

nodes.name: persistReply
nodes.summary: Persists the AI's reply message with token/cost/provider metadata, tolerating a duplicate-insert race by falling back to the existing row.

nodes.name: conversationIsHumanOwned
nodes.summary: Checks whether a conversation has been marked human-owned (AI disabled), used to short-circuit AI turns once a PT has taken over.

nodes.name: notifyManualReply
nodes.summary: Sends a push notification to the PT when the assistant is skipped or escalates, swallowing and logging any notification-dispatch failure so it never blocks the conversation turn.

nodes.name: escalateToHuman
nodes.summary: Dispatches the escalate_to_human tool action to hand a conversation to the PT, treating an already-human-owned conversation as a no-op success.

nodes.name: escalateForSafety
nodes.summary: Escalates a conversation to a human for a detected safety reason and sends the PT a manual-reply notification.

nodes.name: persistSafetyReply
nodes.summary: Persists the deterministic safety-escalation reply text to the patient for a given escalation reason.

nodes.name: logAssistantPausedSkip
nodes.summary: Logs an informational event when a turn is skipped because the PT has manually paused the assistant.

nodes.name: bookedSinceInbound
nodes.summary: Checks whether any appointment was created for the patient after the inbound message arrived, used to pick booking-aware wording on a failed-turn handoff.

nodes.name: runFailedTurnHandoff
nodes.summary: Persists and returns the deterministic handoff reply shown to a patient when a turn could not be completed after retries, choosing wording based on whether the failure left a stray booking.

nodes.name: runTurnCoreUnlocked
nodes.summary: The unlocked core turn implementation: loads context, checks for an existing reply and human ownership, runs safety detection, skips cleanly if the assistant is paused, otherwise loads history and services, builds the system prompt, runs the model turn, and persists the reply or triggers a handoff.

nodes.name: runTurnCore
nodes.summary: Public wrapper that serializes runTurnCoreUnlocked for a given inbound message behind a per-message Postgres advisory lock, preventing concurrent double-processing.

nodes.name: reminderSystemAddendum
nodes.summary: Builds an extra system-prompt section describing the reminder context (appointment ID/time/timezone, ambiguity warning) appended when a turn is triggered by a reminder reply.

nodes.name: runReminderTurn
nodes.summary: Runs a conversation turn triggered by a patient's reply to an appointment reminder, allowing it even on an otherwise-inactive conversation and attributing any resulting cancellation to the patient.

nodes.name: handoffFailedTurn
nodes.summary: Recovery path invoked after every retry of a turn has been exhausted: re-detects safety escalation for correct wording, otherwise persists a neutral or booking-aware technical-failure handoff reply.

nodes.name: runTurn
nodes.summary: Main entry point for handling one inbound WhatsApp message: selects the plan's model and runs the locked, audited core turn, logging (but not swallowing) any failure other than a benign assistant-paused skip.

nodes.name: ConversationEngineError
nodes.summary: Typed Error subclass carrying a closed-set failure code, used throughout the conversation engine to distinguish expected control-flow exits (e.g. assistant paused) from genuine failures.

nodes.name: detectSafetyEscalation
nodes.summary: Classifies a patient message into a safety-escalation reason (human requested, urgent health, legal/billing, insurance, or high frustration) by testing it against curated English/Albanian regex pattern sets, or returns undefined if none match.

nodes.name: safetyEscalationResponse
nodes.summary: Builds the deterministic, non-AI-generated Albanian reply text sent to a patient for a given safety-escalation reason.

nodes.name: loadFunnelWindow
nodes.summary: Loads signup, WhatsApp-connection, first-message, and first-booking counts for a date window, powering the admin funnel view.

nodes.name: loadCohort

nodes.name: loadRolledUpCost

nodes.name: loadTodayLiveCost

nodes.name: loadPushDelivery
nodes.summary: Loads aggregate push-notification delivery counts (sent, removed subscriptions, dispatch attempts) since a given time.

nodes.name: withTimeout

nodes.name: getAdminMetrics
nodes.summary: Assembles the full admin dashboard payload (funnel windows, onboarding cohort, cost summaries, push delivery) by running the underlying loaders in parallel, each bounded by a timeout.

nodes.name: loadPlanDistribution

nodes.name: loadConversion
nodes.summary: Computes free-to-Solo conversion metrics (counts and days-to-convert) for the admin billing dashboard.

nodes.name: loadRenewalRate
nodes.summary: Computes the Solo plan renewal rate around expiry events for the admin billing dashboard.

nodes.name: loadDowngrades
nodes.summary: Computes counts of PTs who downgraded from Solo to Free, for the admin billing dashboard.

nodes.name: loadCapHits

nodes.name: loadRecentPayments

nodes.name: getBillingMetrics
nodes.summary: Assembles the full admin billing dashboard payload (plan distribution, conversion, renewal rate, downgrades, cap hits, free-tier COGS, recent payments) by running the underlying loaders in parallel, bounded by a timeout.

nodes.name: getClientDirectory

nodes.name: getClientDetail

nodes.name: realtime.test.ts

nodes.name: realtime.ts

nodes.name: useRealtimeChannel

nodes.name: useCatchUpRefresh
nodes.summary: Internal helper that triggers a throttled refresh callback whenever the realtime channel reconnects, the tab becomes visible again, or the page is restored from the back/forward cache, so missed updates are caught up on regardless of the trigger source.

nodes.name: useRealtimeRefresh

nodes.name: useMessages
nodes.summary: Maintains a chat thread's message list as a keyed map merged from server-rendered initial messages and live insert/update/delete events, sorted by a Postgres-text-tolerant timestamp comparator and kept fresh via catch-up refresh.

nodes.name: useOnlineStatus

nodes.name: client-store.ts
nodes.summary: Browser-side IndexedDB-backed mutation queue for the offline-first PWA: enqueues appointment/message mutations, attempts to send them immediately when online, replays the queue on reconnect, and exposes queue-changed/synced/failed events for the UI to react to.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the `idb` wrapper over IndexedDB to persist a durable client-side outbox, following an outbox pattern so writes survive page reloads and network drops.

nodes.name: browserDb
nodes.summary: Opens (and lazily creates on first run) the browser's `pwa-store` IndexedDB database with a `pendingMutations` object store indexed by status and creation time.

nodes.name: enqueueMutation
nodes.summary: Persists a new mutation to IndexedDB with a generated id, pending status, and retry count, enforcing a max queue size before writing and registering background sync so it can be flushed even if the tab closes.

nodes.name: retryMutation
nodes.summary: Resets a failed mutation back to pending status and immediately attempts to replay the queue, used when the user manually retries a failed offline action.

nodes.name: sendOrQueueMutation
nodes.summary: Central entry point for all offline-aware writes: enqueues the mutation, attempts to POST it immediately, and on success removes it from the queue or on failure leaves it queued for later replay — returning a result the caller can use to update the UI optimistically.

nodes.name: replayPendingMutations
nodes.summary: Walks the IndexedDB queue in creation order and re-POSTs each pending mutation, removing successes, marking permanent failures, and leaving retryable failures queued — called on reconnect and background sync.

nodes.name: postMutation
nodes.summary: Sends a single mutation payload to its PWA mutation API endpoint and normalizes the fetch/JSON-parse failure paths into a consistent result shape.

nodes.name: clearPwaData
nodes.summary: Wipes all local PWA state on sign-out or account deletion: clears the IndexedDB mutation queue, service-worker caches, and the push-notification opt-out flag.

nodes.name: registerBackgroundSync
nodes.summary: Registers a background-sync tag with the active service worker, when the Background Sync API is supported, so queued mutations flush automatically once connectivity returns.

nodes.name: mutation-client.ts

nodes.name: queueMessageSend
nodes.summary: Builds and queues a send-message mutation with a generated client mutation id, delegating to sendOrQueueMutation and normalizing the response into a client-friendly result.

nodes.name: queueAppointmentMutation
nodes.summary: Builds and queues an appointment mutation (book/reschedule/cancel) with a generated client mutation id, delegating to sendOrQueueMutation.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Normalizes the raw send-or-queue result into a consistent status/clientMutationId shape the PWA UI can branch on regardless of whether the mutation was sent, queued, or failed.

nodes.name: reconcilePushSubscription
nodes.summary: Verifies an existing push subscription is still owned by the current account server-side, unsubscribing and re-subscribing with a fresh VAPID key if ownership can't be confirmed, unless the user has explicitly opted out.

nodes.name: unsubscribeFromPush
nodes.summary: Sets the local opt-out flag and unsubscribes the device's push subscription, removing the corresponding record from the server.

nodes.name: confirm-phrase.ts

nodes.name: completePwaMutation

nodes.name: failPwaMutation

nodes.name: recordPwaMutationProgress
nodes.summary: Merges an incremental progress payload into the mutation's stored result JSON without changing its status, for UI feedback during long-running mutations.

nodes.name: discardPwaMutation
nodes.summary: Deletes a mutation row outright, letting the client retry the action from scratch.

nodes.name: getFreeSlotsInternal
nodes.summary: Generates the grid of bookable slots for a date range by intersecting weekday working-hours rules with blocked periods and existing appointments, deduplicating and timezone-normalizing each candidate slot.

nodes.name: isSlotBookable
nodes.summary: Checks whether an exact start/end interval sits wholly inside one working-hours rule and overlaps no blocked period or active appointment, validating the interval directly rather than grid membership so non-standard service durations aren't wrongly rejected.

nodes.name: findExisting
nodes.summary: Looks up an existing pending/confirmed appointment matching a booking request's practice, patient, and start time, used to make bookAppointment idempotent on replay.

nodes.name: assertPatientBelongsToPractice
nodes.summary: Verifies the patient exists under the given practice before allowing a booking, throwing AppointmentError('not_found') otherwise.

nodes.name: bookAppointment
nodes.summary: Validates booking input, acquires a per-practice advisory lock, checks slot availability, inserts the appointment and its booked event in one transaction, publishes the outbox event, and gracefully resolves concurrent duplicate-key races to the same appointment.

nodes.name: cancelAppointment
nodes.summary: Cancels an appointment by delegating to transitionAppointment with nextStatus 'cancelled', forwarding the cancelling actor and reason.

nodes.name: AppointmentError

nodes.name: withAppointmentLock
nodes.summary: Runs a callback under a Postgres advisory lock keyed by practice id, serializing all appointment mutations for that practice.

nodes.name: rescheduleAppointment
nodes.summary: Moves an active appointment to a new start time: validates the new slot is bookable, re-locks the row inside a transaction, updates the times, appends a rescheduled event with from/to timestamps, and maps unique/exclusion constraint violations to a conflict error.

nodes.name: assertAppointmentTransition
nodes.summary: Enforces the appointment status state machine, allowing same-state no-ops and throwing AppointmentError('invalid_transition') for any transition outside the allow-list.

nodes.languageNotes: Uses AsyncLocalStorage to detect reentrant lock acquisition within the same async call chain, so nested locks (e.g. an AI turn holding a conversation lock while its tool calls take an appointment lock) reuse the outer transaction instead of each reserving a pooled connection and deadlocking.

nodes.summary: Orchestrates deterministic handling of inbound WhatsApp replies to appointment reminders — confirm, cancel, reschedule, opt-out, and opt-in — matching the reply to the right pending reminder job, applying the appointment mutation, and persisting an idempotent reply, all under a per-message advisory lock.
nodes.languageNotes: Extensive comments address Inngest's at-least-once, non-FIFO delivery guarantees — e.g. optStateSuperseded prevents an out-of-order opt-out/opt-in retry pair from leaving the patient in the wrong final state.

nodes.name: withAdvisoryLock
nodes.summary: Acquires a Postgres advisory lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock) scoped to the calling transaction, reusing the enclosing transaction on a reentrant call instead of opening a second connection, and enforcing a bounded lock_timeout so a contended key errors instead of blocking forever.

nodes.name: findExistingReply
nodes.summary: Looks up an already-persisted AI reply to a given inbound message, making reminder response handling idempotent under Inngest retries.

nodes.name: persistReminderReply
nodes.summary: Inserts the deterministic reminder reply message, tolerating a conflicting concurrent insert by returning the reply that won instead of throwing.

nodes.name: loadReminderCandidates
nodes.summary: Fetches the sent reminder jobs still eligible to be answered by an inbound message — active or already resolved by that same message — bounded to a 48-hour response window so a stale unanswered reminder can't hijack a later reply.

nodes.name: recordReminderResponse
nodes.summary: Records a reminder job's response type and responding message, guarded so it only overwrites an unanswered job, the same retried message, or a reschedule follow-up.

nodes.name: reminderTurnContext
nodes.summary: Builds the ReminderTurnContext handed to the AI fallback turn when a reminder reply can't be resolved deterministically, carrying the candidate appointment's details when one exists.

nodes.name: optStateSuperseded
nodes.summary: Checks whether a newer patient message already requested the opposite opt-in/opt-out state, so an out-of-order Inngest retry of an older message doesn't overwrite a state the patient has since changed.

nodes.name: setReminderOptOut
nodes.summary: Marks a patient as opted out of automated reminders, using COALESCE so a repeated NDAL doesn't overwrite the original opt-out timestamp.

nodes.name: clearReminderOptOut
nodes.summary: Clears a patient's reminder opt-out flag on an explicit opt-in, returning whether a row actually changed so the reply can distinguish a real reactivation from an already-active state.

nodes.name: handleConfirm
nodes.summary: Handles a confirm reply: transitions the appointment to confirmed, records the reminder response, and sends a confirmation reply with the formatted appointment time.

nodes.name: handleCancel
nodes.summary: Handles a cancel reply: cancels the appointment using the patient's message as the recorded reason, records the reminder response, and replies confirming the cancellation with an invitation to pick a new time.

nodes.name: handleOptOut
nodes.summary: Handles an opt-out reply: sets the opt-out flag unless a newer message already superseded it, optionally records the response against a candidate reminder, and replies with the AKTIVIZO keyword needed to opt back in.

nodes.name: handleOptIn
nodes.summary: Handles an opt-in reply: clears the opt-out flag and persists the reply in a single transaction so a crash between the two steps can't strand the patient without confirmation, wording the reply differently if reminders were already active.

nodes.name: handleReschedule
nodes.summary: Handles a reschedule reply: records the request, fetches up to five alternative free slots over the next week excluding the current appointment, and replies with a numbered list or a no-availability message.

nodes.name: chooseCandidate
nodes.summary: Selects the single reminder job an inbound reply should resolve against, preferring unresponded jobs over reschedule follow-ups, and signals an ambiguous-reminders fallback when more than one candidate ties.

nodes.name: handleReminderResponseUnlocked
nodes.summary: Main dispatch for an inbound reminder reply: replays an existing reply if present, parses intent, resolves opt-out/opt-in independent of any candidate, otherwise picks a candidate reminder and routes to confirm/cancel/reschedule or falls back to the AI turn when intent or candidate is unclear.

nodes.name: handleReminderResponse

nodes.name: safe-next.ts
nodes.summary: Sanitises the post-auth next redirect target so auth routes never issue an open redirect, resolving the value against a probe origin rather than relying on a character-class check alone.

nodes.name: 0000_init_extensions.sql
nodes.summary: Bootstrap migration enabling the pgcrypto Postgres extension, which provides gen_random_uuid() used as the default primary key generator for every table in the schema.

nodes.name: appointments
nodes.summary: Core scheduling table holding one row per booked visit: patient/PT pair, time range, status lifecycle (pending/confirmed/cancelled/no_show/completed/rescheduled), and free-text service type and notes.

nodes.name: audit_log
nodes.summary: Append-only audit trail capturing who (actor) did what (action) to which record (target_table/target_id) and when, scoped per tenant.

nodes.name: availability_rules
nodes.summary: Recurring weekly availability template per PT: a weekday plus a start/end time window used to compute open booking slots.

nodes.name: blocked_periods
nodes.summary: One-off time ranges (holidays, personal blocks) that a PT marks as unavailable for booking, independent of the recurring availability rules.

nodes.name: conversations
nodes.summary: One row per patient-PT messaging thread, tracking the active channel, last inbound message time, whether the AI assistant is currently handling it, and escalation state.

nodes.name: events
nodes.summary: Generic append-only domain event log keyed by pt_id, type, and a JSONB payload, used as the source feed for the outbox/notification pipeline.

nodes.name: message_templates
nodes.summary: WhatsApp Business message template metadata (name, language, Meta approval status, body) that a PT can send as pre-approved outbound messages.

nodes.name: messages
nodes.summary: Every inbound and outbound message in a conversation, including AI-generated replies with token/cost accounting fields (tokens_in/out, cached_tokens, model, provider) and the originating template.

nodes.name: patients
nodes.summary: A PT's patient roster: name, phone, WhatsApp ID, and free-text notes, scoped per tenant.

nodes.name: pts
nodes.summary: The tenant root table, one row per physical therapist account, holding practice identity, timezone, AI assistant persona (name/greeting/escalation keyword), and GDPR retention window; its id is the same UUID as the Supabase auth.users id.

nodes.name: push_subscriptions
nodes.summary: Web Push subscription endpoints and keys registered by a PT's browser/PWA install, used to deliver notifications outside of WhatsApp.

nodes.name: reminder_jobs
nodes.summary: Scheduled appointment-reminder jobs tracked through an Inngest background run, one row per appointment reminder with its delivery status.

nodes.name: whatsapp_connections
nodes.summary: A PT's linked WhatsApp Business Cloud API credentials, phone number ID, WABA ID, encrypted access token, quality tier, and the connection's lifecycle status.

nodes.name: 0002_rls_policies.sql
nodes.summary: Enables Postgres row-level security and installs a symmetric FOR ALL tenant-isolation policy (pt_id = auth.uid(), or id = auth.uid() for pts itself) on all 13 tables from the initial schema, establishing the foundational multi-tenant security boundary later narrowed by migration 0024.

nodes.name: 0003_pts_signup_trigger.sql
nodes.summary: Foreign-keys pts.id to Supabase auth.users.id with ON DELETE CASCADE and installs a SECURITY DEFINER handle_new_user() trigger that auto-provisions a default pts row (Europe/Berlin timezone, 90-day retention) on every new signup.
nodes.languageNotes: SECURITY DEFINER with an explicit SET search_path = public is required so the trigger can insert into public.pts regardless of the invoking role, while avoiding search-path hijacking.

nodes.name: 0004_whatsapp_webhook_indexes.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a unique (pt_id, wa_id) index on patients and a lookup index on whatsapp_connections.phone_number_id to speed up inbound WhatsApp webhook routing to the right tenant.

nodes.name: 0005_whatsapp_connection_unique.sql
nodes.summary: Replaces the plain phone_number_id index on whatsapp_connections with a unique index, guaranteeing at most one connection record per WhatsApp Business phone number.

nodes.name: 0006_ai_conversation_metadata.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a self-referencing reply_to_message_id foreign key and an ai_cost_microusd column to messages, with a partial unique index ensuring each AI reply is linked to at most one source message.

nodes.name: event_outbox
nodes.summary: Transactional outbox table queuing domain events for reliable downstream publishing (attempts, available_at, locked_at, published_at), paired with a GiST exclusion constraint that makes double-booking a PT impossible at the database level.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a PostgreSQL GiST EXCLUDE constraint (via the btree_gist extension) on (pt_id, tstzrange(starts_at, ends_at)) to reject overlapping active appointments transactionally, instead of relying solely on application-level conflict checks.

nodes.name: 0008_phase5_background_jobs.sql
nodes.summary: Extends the reminder pipeline: adds 'requeued'/'skipped' to the reminder_status enum, adds retry/error/timestamp columns to reminder_jobs and audit_log/messages, links reminder_jobs to its sent message, and backfills WhatsApp token expiry for already-active connections.

nodes.name: 0009_phase6_reminders.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a reminder_response_type enum (confirm/cancel/reschedule_requested/opt_out) and wires reminder_jobs to the patient's WhatsApp reply, plus an opt-out timestamp on patients.

nodes.name: 0010_phase7_realtime.sql
nodes.summary: Adds notification-preference columns to pts and enables Supabase Realtime (idempotently creating the supabase_realtime publication and adding appointments/messages/conversations/events) with REPLICA IDENTITY FULL so the PWA can subscribe to live row filters.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses idempotent DO $$ ... $$ PL/pgSQL blocks with a FOREACH loop and EXECUTE format(...) so the migration can run safely whether or not the supabase_realtime publication already exists (hosted Supabase vs. bare local Postgres).

nodes.name: pwa_mutations
nodes.summary: Offline-mutation queue for the PWA's optimistic-sync layer: each row tracks a client-generated mutation ID through processing to success/failure so retried submissions are deduplicated.

nodes.name: whatsapp_contacts
nodes.summary: Synced WhatsApp contact roster used during Cloud API/Coexistence mode migration, tracking sync provenance and soft-deletion; paired with new AI-pause columns on conversations and coexistence sync-state columns on whatsapp_connections.

nodes.name: services
nodes.summary: PT-defined bookable service catalog (name, duration, active flag) backfilled from historical appointment service_type/duration data and seeded with three Albanian-language defaults for new and history-free practices; also extends conversations with read/closed timestamps.
nodes.languageNotes: The backfill uses SELECT DISTINCT ON to pick the most recent historical duration per (pt_id, service name), and a CROSS JOIN ... WHERE NOT EXISTS to seed default services only for practices with no existing rows, both idempotent, re-runnable patterns.

nodes.name: 0014_phase13_review_hardening.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a services_configured_at timestamp to pts and backfills it to now() for all existing tenants, marking their service catalog as already reviewed.

nodes.name: 0015_phase9_push_subscription_unique.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a unique index on push_subscriptions.endpoint to prevent duplicate Web Push registrations for the same browser endpoint.

nodes.name: erasure_archive
nodes.summary: Deny-all, service-role-only compliance ledger recording GDPR erasure events (scope, target, a hash of the pre-erasure state) so a deletion can be proven to have happened without retaining the erased data itself.
nodes.languageNotes: RLS policy uses USING (false) to deny all tenant access rather than a tenant-scoped predicate; the table is written only by the service-role connection, which bypasses RLS entirely.

nodes.name: cost_daily
nodes.summary: Per-tenant daily cost rollup combining AI inference spend (ai_cost_microusd, cached tokens) and Meta conversation billing (meta_conversations, meta_cost_micro_eur), computed by a daily cron job.

nodes.name: 0018_phase15_settings_fields.sql
nodes.summary: Adds PT profile fields (full_name, title, address, assistant_paused) and a services.price_lek column with a positive-price check constraint, plus a display_phone_number on whatsapp_connections.

nodes.name: 0019_sudden_weapon_omega.sql
nodes.summary: Adds four IF-NOT-EXISTS lookup indexes (appointments by pt/created, events by type/occurred, messages by pt/created and by created alone) intended to be applied CONCURRENTLY in production to avoid locking the messages table.
nodes.languageNotes: The migration comment documents a real operational split: this file uses plain CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS for safe use in transactional test/local runs, while production deployments must first run the same indexes with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY outside a transaction to avoid write locks on a large table.

nodes.name: conversation_days
nodes.summary: Metering fact table counting one row per patient-day a conversation was active, keyed by (pt_id, patient_id, local_day), used to enforce and display the Free-plan monthly conversation cap; introduced alongside the pts.plan/plan_expires_at billing columns.

nodes.name: wa_message_statuses
nodes.summary: Deny-all operator ledger of Meta delivery-status callbacks per outbound WhatsApp message (sent/delivered/read/failed timestamps, billing category/type/model), the source of truth for Meta conversation billing; adds matching cost/delivery columns to cost_daily and reminder_jobs.

nodes.name: billing_orders
nodes.summary: The POK payment-provider order ledger: one row per checkout attempt with plan/period/amount, lifecycle status (created/paid/failed/expired), and the plan-expiry window it purchased; read-only to tenants via a FOR SELECT-only RLS policy since all writes go through the RLS-bypassing owner connection.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately omits INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies for authenticated users on a money ledger; the repo's later migration 0024 generalizes this read-own, write-never posture to the rest of the schema.

nodes.name: 0023_violet_meteorite.sql
nodes.summary: Security fix reverting REPLICA IDENTITY FULL back to DEFAULT on seven tables (messages, conversations, appointments, events, patients, reminder_jobs, services): Supabase Realtime does not apply column filters to DELETE events, so FULL was broadcasting entire deleted rows, including patient health data and PII, to every authenticated subscriber across tenants.

nodes.name: 0024_tenant_read_only_rls.sql
nodes.summary: Major security hardening migration: revokes INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE from anon/authenticated across the whole public schema and narrows the FOR ALL tenant-isolation policy to FOR SELECT on 21 tables, closing a PostgREST write path that would have let a tenant self-grant a paid plan, erase their audit trail, or forge trusted event_outbox rows.
nodes.languageNotes: Documents the actual attack surface being closed (self-granting billing plan, erasing audit_log, forging event_outbox rows) rather than just the mechanical DDL, and establishes the repo convention that new tables get GRANT SELECT only, never GRANT ALL.

nodes.name: 0025_conversation_days_survive_erasure.sql
nodes.summary: Makes conversation_days.patient_id and conversation_id nullable with ON DELETE SET NULL (instead of CASCADE) so GDPR patient erasure or conversation retention purges anonymize the metering row instead of deleting it, preventing a PT from reclaiming Free-plan quota by erasing chatty patients.
nodes.languageNotes: Trades a hard CASCADE delete for ON DELETE SET NULL specifically to let a billing-relevant fact outlive the personal data it was originally attached to, a pattern repeated in migration 0026 for reminder_deliveries.

nodes.name: reminder_deliveries
nodes.summary: Splits metered reminder-delivery counting out of reminder_jobs.delivered_at into its own append-only table (one row per Meta-confirmed wamid), fixing both a GDPR erasure quota-reset bug and a reschedule under-counting bug where a second billed template overwrote the first delivery record.
nodes.languageNotes: appointment_id is nullable with ON DELETE SET NULL so the billing fact survives appointment/patient deletion; external_id (the wamid) is rewritten to 'erased:<row id>' on patient erasure since a wamid embeds the recipient's phone number and is not itself anonymous.

nodes.name: 0027_revoke_reference_and_trigger_grants.sql
nodes.summary: Closes a residual privilege gap left by 0024: revokes REFERENCES, TRIGGER, and (version-gated) MAINTAIN from anon/authenticated on all public tables, removing an unused but theoretically dangerous privilege-escalation primitive where a tenant-owned trigger function would run with the table owner's RLS-bypassing rights.
nodes.languageNotes: Guards the PG17-only REVOKE MAINTAIN statement behind a server_version_num check inside a DO $$ block so the migration doesn't abort on older Postgres servers where the privilege doesn't exist.

nodes.name: 0008_snapshot.json

nodes.name: 0009_snapshot.json

nodes.name: 0010_snapshot.json
nodes.summary: Schema snapshot for the 0010_phase7_realtime migration, keeping the 14-table, 7-enum schema while enabling realtime-related database changes to support live updates in the PWA.

nodes.name: 0011_snapshot.json

nodes.name: 0012_snapshot.json

nodes.name: 0013_snapshot.json

nodes.name: 0014_snapshot.json

nodes.name: 0015_snapshot.json
nodes.summary: Schema snapshot for the 0015_phase9_push_subscription_unique migration, adding a uniqueness constraint on push subscriptions without changing the 17-table, 9-enum schema inventory.

nodes.name: 0016_snapshot.json
nodes.summary: Schema snapshot for the 0016_phase10_gdpr migration, adding the erasure_archive table (18 tables total) to support GDPR-style right-to-erasure data retention.

nodes.name: 0017_snapshot.json

nodes.name: 0018_snapshot.json

nodes.name: 0020_snapshot.json
nodes.summary: Drizzle ORM schema snapshot capturing the full PostgreSQL schema state after migration 0020 (steep_rattler): 20 tables and 10 enums, adding the `plan` enum and `conversation_days` table plus new subscription-plan columns (plan, plan_expires_at, plan_lifetime, plan_downgraded_at, plan_step_seen_at) on `pts`.
nodes.languageNotes: Drizzle-kit snapshots are auto-generated on every `drizzle-kit generate` run; each one captures the complete schema so the next generate can diff against it instead of replaying every prior migration.

nodes.name: 0021_snapshot.json
nodes.summary: Schema snapshot after migration 0021 (simple_silk_fever): grows to 21 tables by adding `wa_message_statuses` for WhatsApp Business API delivery-status tracking, plus Meta billing columns on `cost_daily` and a `delivered_at` column on `reminder_jobs`.

nodes.name: 0023_snapshot.json
nodes.summary: Schema snapshot after migration 0023 (violet_meteorite): same 22 tables and 12 enums as the prior snapshot, recording a new composite index on `messages` and REPLICA IDENTITY DEFAULT enabled on core tables (messages, conversations, appointments, events, patients, reminder_jobs, services) to support Postgres logical replication for realtime features.

nodes.languageNotes: Combines a schema-wide REVOKE with per-table RLS policies as defense-in-depth: even if a policy is misconfigured, the role-level grant revocation still blocks writes from anon/authenticated.

nodes.name: 0025_snapshot.json

nodes.name: 0026_snapshot.json

nodes.name: 0027_snapshot.json

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to get oriented: Medium is a multi-tenant SaaS that lets solo physical therapists manage patient bookings over WhatsApp, backed by an AI assistant and overseen from a mobile-first PWA. Its "current scope" section describes an early bootstrap scaffold, but as this tour will show, the actual codebase has grown into a substantial production system spanning billing, WhatsApp integration, AI conversation handling, and strict multi-tenant data isolation. Keep that gap in mind as a reminder to trust the code over the docs when the two disagree.

tour.title: Application Shell & Routing
tour.description: Three Next.js App Router conventions work together as the closest thing this app has to a single entry point: `middleware.ts` refreshes the Supabase session cookie on every request while still letting public pages through when auth isn't configured, `app/layout.tsx` wraps every page in the shared HTML shell with PWA metadata and fonts, and `app/page.tsx` is the root route that redirects signed-in PTs to `/today` or renders the landing page for everyone else. There's no traditional `main()` here because Next.js's file-based routing makes every route file its own entry point.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router treats `layout.tsx`, `page.tsx`, and root `middleware.ts` as framework-invoked convention files rather than manually imported modules — that's why they show almost no fan-in in the dependency graph despite being the literal entry points of every request.

tour.title: Data Model & Database Client
tour.description: `lib/db/schema.ts` (132 incoming references) is the Drizzle ORM schema defining every table in the system: PTs (the tenant root), patients, WhatsApp connections, conversations, messages, appointments, availability, reminders, billing orders, and the event outbox. `lib/db/index.ts` (135 references, the single most-imported file in the codebase) initializes the shared Postgres client as an HMR-safe singleton tuned for Supabase's connection pooler, and exports the typed `db` instance that nearly every module in this tour depends on. Understanding these two files first makes everything downstream legible.
tour.languageLesson: Caching a database client on `globalThis` in development (an "HMR-safe singleton") stops Next.js's hot module reloading from opening a fresh Postgres connection pool on every file save.

tour.title: Multi-Tenancy Enforcement
tour.description: Because one PT's data must never leak into another PT's dashboard, the tenancy module is the application-layer half of that guarantee. `lib/tenancy/service-client.ts` is described in its own summary as "the single choke point stopping malformed tenant ids from reaching queries," validating that a `ptId` is a well-formed UUID before any query runs. `lib/tenancy/audit.ts` wraps mutations with an audit-log write scoped to that same `ptId`, and `lib/tenancy/index.ts` is the public barrel re-exporting both alongside the authenticated client factory. Building on the schema from Step 3, this is the pattern that keeps every PT's patients, appointments, and messages isolated.

tour.title: Row-Level Security Migrations
tour.description: The application-layer checks from Step 4 are backed by a second, independent line of defense inside Postgres itself. The `pts` table (28 references) is the tenant root: one row per physical therapist, whose id is literally shared with the Supabase `auth.users` id. Migration `0002_rls_policies.sql` enables row-level security and installs a symmetric tenant-isolation policy across all 13 initial tables, and migration `0024_tenant_read_only_rls.sql` later hardens that policy by revoking direct writes through PostgREST entirely, closing a path that would have let a tenant self-grant a paid plan or erase their own audit trail.
tour.languageLesson: This is defense in depth: application code validates tenant ids before querying (Step 4), while RLS policies enforce the same boundary independently inside the database — so a bug in one layer doesn't expose another tenant's data.

tour.title: Dashboard Shell & Read Models
tour.description: `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` is the root layout for every authenticated screen: it guards auth and onboarding completion, fetches practice, notification, and unread-chat data in parallel, and wraps every dashboard page in shared chrome. It leans heavily on `lib/pwa/read-models.ts`, a central aggregation layer that assembles calendar, chat-thread, chat-list, and settings snapshots by combining the schema from Step 3 with billing entitlements and WhatsApp connection state into one serializable shape used across nearly every dashboard page. This read-model layer is so central that the graph analysis flags it as part of the codebase's most tightly coupled cluster, alongside the chat query layer and the database client from Step 3.

tour.title: WhatsApp Channel Integration
tour.description: This is the product's primary channel: patients interact with their PT entirely through WhatsApp. `app/api/webhooks/whatsapp/route.ts` is the central inbound webhook — it verifies Meta's signature and dispatches each change type (new messages, delivery statuses, history sync, account updates) to a dedicated handler. `lib/channels/whatsapp/client.ts` handles the outbound side, wrapping Meta's Graph API to decrypt a stored token, send messages and templates, and revoke a connection on fatal auth errors. Together they form the two-way bridge between a PT's WhatsApp Business account and the tenant-scoped data model from Steps 3-5.

tour.title: AI Conversation Engine
tour.description: Every inbound WhatsApp message from Step 7 is ultimately handed to `lib/conversation/engine.ts`, the orchestrator that loads conversation context, runs a multi-step LLM turn with tool-calling under an advisory lock, and routes the result to safety escalation, human handoff, or a reminder-triggered turn. Before the AI ever responds, `lib/conversation/safety.ts` runs a deterministic, regex-based check for messages that must escalate to a human — urgent symptoms, legal or billing disputes, or high frustration — tuned for both English and diacritic-variant Albanian text. This safety-first design reflects a real product constraint: the AI is a scheduling assistant, not a clinical one, so escalation has to be reliable and independent of the LLM's own judgment.

tour.title: AI Tool-Calling & Booking
tour.description: When the conversation engine from Step 8 decides to act rather than just reply, it calls into `lib/ai/tools.ts`, which defines Zod-validated tool schemas (get_availability, book_appointment, reschedule_appointment, cancel_appointment, escalate_to_human) exposed to the LLM, and `lib/ai/dispatcher.ts`, which executes those tool calls against real domain logic, audit-logging each one and translating errors into patient-safe Albanian responses. The domain logic underneath is `lib/appointments/book.ts`, which runs booking under a per-practice advisory lock and replays idempotently on race conditions, and `lib/appointments/availability.ts`, which computes free slots from working-hours rules, blocked periods, and existing appointments with full timezone and DST handling. This is the seam where natural-language conversation turns into transactional, tenant-scoped database writes.
tour.languageLesson: Zod schemas do double duty here as both runtime validation and the tool-call contract the LLM sees — the same schema that rejects malformed input also documents to the model what arguments a tool accepts.

tour.title: Billing & POK Payments
tour.description: `lib/billing/plans.ts` is the single source of truth for the Free and Solo plan limits, prices, and per-plan AI model configuration, while `lib/billing/entitlements.ts` resolves a PT's effective plan and message-retention window using pure, database-free functions that account for lifetime access and downgrade grace periods. Payment processing runs through POK rather than Stripe: `lib/billing/pok/client.ts` wraps the POK SDK for order creation and capture, and `app/api/webhooks/pok/route.ts` receives POK's payment webhook, which deliberately does nothing but re-validate the order and always return 200 so POK never retries delivery. This POK-specific integration reflects a real market constraint — standard payment providers aren't available in Albania.

tour.title: Background Jobs & Event Outbox
tour.description: Many actions from earlier steps — sending a WhatsApp reminder, renewing a billing period, rolling up daily AI costs — happen asynchronously through Inngest. `lib/inngest/client.ts` instantiates the shared client, and `lib/inngest/functions.ts` is the central registry aggregating every background job handler into the array the Inngest API route serves. Rather than calling Inngest directly from request handlers, domain code writes to `lib/events/outbox.ts`, a transactional-outbox implementation that claims due events with a SQL-level lock, validates them against a schema registry, forwards them to Inngest, and applies exponential backoff with a dead-letter cutoff on repeated failures.
tour.languageLesson: The transactional outbox pattern avoids the classic "dual write" problem: instead of writing to the database and publishing an event as two operations that could fail independently, the event is written to an outbox table in the same transaction, then a separate process reliably delivers it afterward.

tour.title: Offline PWA & Localization
tour.description: Because PTs use this as an installed mobile PWA that may lose connectivity mid-visit, `lib/pwa/mutation-store.ts` tracks every offline-first mutation (booking or messaging actions) through processing, success, and failed states, and allows exactly one reclaim of a stale in-flight row so a flaky connection can't cause a WhatsApp message to be sent twice. Every piece of UI text these mutations surface flows through `lib/i18n/index.ts`, the app's i18n entry point — currently a single Albanian locale, split into per-feature dictionaries for appointments, billing, chat, settings, and more, keeping translations colocated with the features that use them. With 91 incoming references, this i18n module is one of the most widely used files in the entire codebase.

tour.title: Testing Multi-Tenant Isolation
tour.description: With tenant isolation enforced at two independent layers (application checks in Step 4, RLS policies in Step 5), `tests/rls/isolation.integration.test.ts` is what actually proves it holds. It runs a comprehensive matrix that, for every tenant-scoped table, verifies user A can only ever select their own rows and that direct writes through PostgREST are rejected outright regardless of ownership. It even includes a registry test ensuring every tenant table has a seed factory and update-column mapping, specifically so a newly added table can't silently ship without RLS coverage — the kind of test suite you'd expect from a codebase that treats tenant isolation as a hard security requirement, not a nice-to-have.

tour.title: Configuration & Developer Workflow
tour.description: `.env.example` is the master template enumerating every external credential this app needs — Supabase, Meta/WhatsApp embedded signup, OpenRouter AI models, Inngest, VAPID web push, and token encryption keys — and `package.json` defines the scripts tying the toolchain together, including Drizzle migrations and seeding, Vitest unit/integration suites, and Husky pre-commit hooks. `supabase/config.toml` configures the local Supabase CLI stack (Postgres, GoTrue auth, Studio) that integration tests run against, matching the local-stack setup described in the README from Step 1. Finally, `AGENTS.md` documents the actual day-to-day workflow for anyone contributing to this repo: check the task tracker, read the current phase's checklist, implement, test, then update the tracker.
